title: Rollouts 1.47x faster, identical
text: Profile (gprof, teacher-label games): c2's forward pass 61%, helper features 37% (draw_dist 14, de_count via de_score 11, rl_helpers 7), engine 3%. Rewrote draw_dist over reachable cells only, the hand convolution over non-zero terms, de_score in one pass: 66 -> 97 rollouts/s per process under the same load, checksum and whole teacher games identical. Now the net is 77%. Machine ceiling measured idle: 1 process 334 rollouts/s, 4 processes 1,070 in total, 8 processes 1,020 (hyperthreads add nothing).
A: today's advisor teacher (128 draws, rollouts to the end)
G: A + the teacher also grades card choices inside my own actions (Workshop / Artisan / Remodel / Mine gains, trashes, Throne Room, Cellar)

title: Full rollouts, more draws, gate margin 0.01 z 1
text: On the 240-position bank: c2 alone 0.88 points of regret per decision; today's teacher 0.57; 320 draws (3 processes) 0.47 at today's gate and 0.38 at margin 0.01 / z 1, smooth over the gate grid. Value-net leaves stop improving at 0.48-0.50 (640 and 1,600 draws alike): the value net's bias is the floor. Arm H (320 draws, new gate, card choices) is the deployment candidate, paired with A on stream ts1.
rejected: Leaves (no gain past their bias floor); the single best gate cell (margin 0.01, z 0: 0.34 at 320 draws but 0.54 at 128, fragile when the laptop is busy).

text: H: the deployment candidate -- the advisor with 3 processes (~320 draws), the gate the bank chose (margin 0.01, z 1), card choices

title: Decision bank instead of screening arms
text: A and B both score about 62% against c2 and differ by -0.8 points [-10, +8] after 61 kingdoms: 300 kingdoms resolve only about +-4 points, while settings differ by 1-3. Settings that only change how accurately the teacher reads rollout values (leaves, halving, draw budget, gate) are now judged on a bank of 240 positions graded with 2,048 full rollouts (regret at equal time); matches are kept for card choices (arm G = A + card choices) and the final confirmation. B stopped at 61 kingdoms.
rejected: Arms C-F (halving, leaves 8 and 2) on 200 kingdoms each: two days of compute for intervals too wide to choose.

text: B: value-net leaves after 4 turns, 5x the draws in about the same time

title: Screening arms on 200 kingdoms
text: Arms C-F (halving, leaves + halving, leaves 8, leaves 2) play the first 200 kingdoms of stream ts1, paired game for game with A and B on the same kingdoms; the winner is then confirmed on a fresh stream at the advisor's real budget.
rejected: 300 kingdoms each: 2 lanes x 2 arms would end Thursday evening, leaving too little time to confirm and deploy.

title: Leaf check
text: Value-net leaves after 2/4/8 turns cost 0.08/0.20/0.39 of a full rollout and rank options within a position with correlation 0.80/0.87/0.93 to full rollouts (128 draws each, so part of the gap is the reference's own noise). The value's sign and level agree with real outcomes (correlation 0.97-0.99).

title: Improve the search, not the net
text: Four days go to the teacher's search: value-net leaves, successive halving, several processes in the advisor and the override gate, each as a match arm at the advisor's time budget against frozen c2. The teacher is the strongest model (59-62% vs c2) and sg-v1 showed further PPO from c2 is flat.
rejected: Training a new net (PPO / distilling the teacher): sg-v1 and bv-v1's student found no gain in days of compute.

title: Compare arms at equal time, run side by side
text: Arms A (today's teacher: 128 draws to the end) and B (value leaves after 4 turns, 640 draws, about the same time) run at once with 4 workers each on the same kingdom order, so they can be compared on the same kingdoms at any point.
rejected: One arm after another with 7 workers: the second answer would come ~10 hours after the first.
